subject: Critical Thinking
subcategory: Evidence & Truth: How We Know What's Real
title: The Limits of Empiricism
description: A quick win: understand The Limits of Empiricism.

hook.text: David Hume woke up one morning and realized he couldn't prove the sun would rise.

buildup.text: Empiricism says all knowledge comes from experience. But experience only tells us what has happened, not what must.

discovery.text: The problem of induction: no amount of observed sunrises logically guarantees the next one.

twist.text: Science relies on induction daily — yet Hume showed it has no logical foundation. We trust patterns, not proofs.

climax.text: Karl Popper's solution: we can't prove theories true, only falsify them. Science advances by elimination.

punchline.text: Every sunrise is an act of faith in patterns.

quiz.question: What is the 'problem of induction' identified by Hume?
options: Past observations can't logically guarantee future outcomes

details.summary: Empiricism cannot answer all questions. Ethical values, mathematical truths, consciousness, and the existence of other minds lie beyond what observation and experiment can settle.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing empiricism's limits prevents scientism — the belief that science can answer all meaningful questions — while still respecting its power within its domain.
takeaways: Empiricism cannot determine moral values or obligations
Mathematical and logical truths exist independently of observation
Consciousness and subjective experience resist empirical analysis

faq.question: What is scientism and why is it considered a problem?
faq.answer: Scientism is the belief that scientific methods can answer all meaningful questions. It is problematic because it dismisses ethics, aesthetics, and meaning as unimportant simply because they cannot be measured in a laboratory.

faq.question: What types of truths can reason discover that empiricism cannot?
faq.answer: Mathematical proofs, logical tautologies, and conceptual truths are known through reason alone. That 2+2=4 requires no experiment. These a priori truths demonstrate that not all knowledge depends on observation.
